title: Citizenship Tier Statutes: Rights by Rank
body:
Meridian 88 operates under the Unified Citizenship Classification Act of 2171, which formally codified what had been an informal corporate practice into binding megacity law. Citizens are assigned one of five tiers — Sovereign, Corporate, Registered, Provisional, and Unclassified — each carrying a distinct bundle of legal rights, service entitlements, and liability protections. The classification is not purely economic; it is a legal status that determines which courts can hear your case, which enforcement agencies are obligated to respond to your calls, and whether your biometric data is subject to mandatory third-party licensing. The Act was drafted by a consortium of eleven corponations and ratified by the Meridian Civic Assembly, which at the time had a supermajority of corporate-bloc delegates.

Sovereign-tier citizens — approximately 0.3% of Meridian's population — are exclusively senior corponation executives, major shareholders, and their immediate family dependents. They are exempt from standard customs searches at any of Meridian's eleven transit hubs, including the O'Hare Consolidated Gateway and the Kenosha Deepwater Port. Their legal disputes are handled by the Meridian Arbitration Chamber on the 91st floor of the Lakeshore Apex Tower, a venue that has never published a public docket. Sovereign-tier individuals cannot be detained by municipal enforcement without a warrant co-signed by a Circuit Arbiter and the corponation's registered legal counsel.

Registered-tier citizens — the largest formal class, roughly 41% of the population — are employees of licensed mid-tier companies, skilled independents who have passed the Meridian Skills Certification Board, and long-term residents with clean compliance records. They have access to the public transit grid, can petition Civic Courts, and are entitled to emergency medical response within a contractually mandated 22-minute window. However, their neural interface data is subject to routine audit by the Regional Compliance Authority if flagged by an algorithmic review system called SENTRY-4, which generates approximately 19,000 audit triggers per day across the megacity.

Provisional and Unclassified residents — together comprising nearly 28% of the population — exist in a legal gray zone that the Act's drafters described, without apparent irony, as a 'pathway structure.' Provisional residents have a rolling 90-day compliance window to demonstrate economic participation or face reclassification downward to Unclassified status. Unclassified persons have no standing in Civic Courts, no guaranteed emergency response, and no right to contest their own biometric data usage. They can be relocated from designated Corporate Zones under the Urban Coherence Ordinance with 48 hours' notice — a provision used approximately 3,400 times in 2199 alone, primarily in the Pilsen Corridor and the North Shore Buffer District.
